text: The retrieved literature offers only limited direct coverage of the study's hypotheses. Lazer et al. (2018) frame fake news as a multidisciplinary problem, noting that the type and source of information shape how audiences evaluate its credibility, which is broadly consistent with H1 and H2. Gigerenzer and Gaissmaier (2010) describe heuristics as efficient processes that ignore part of the available information, providing a mechanism by which information type could influence plausibility judgments (H2). Beyond these, the remaining works address topics (tourism climate, energy acceptance, immigration prejudice, brand psychology, etc.) that do not speak directly to information-type effects on sharing or plausibility.

works.title: Weather and Climate Information for Tourism
works.abstract: The tourism sector is one of the largest and fastest growing global industries and is a significant contributor to national and local economies around the world. The interface between climate and tourism is multifaceted and complex, as climate represents both a vital resource to be exploited and an important limiting factor that poses risks to be managed by the tourism industry and tourists alike.
